prospect.name: Dhairya Nanda
prospect.occupation: Office-based / hybrid professional; works from home most days, goes in for meetings. Specific role never stated.
prospect.family_status: Engaged, wedding in December; fiancee currently living in New York; no children
prospect.training_background: Trains at an apartment gym on machines, mostly upper body (chest, triceps, biceps). Push-ups fine, struggles with pull-ups, core and body-weight work and HIIT circuits. Says lower-body strength is 'in a very bad shape'. Has bought generic online subscriptions before with no follow-up. Rates current physique 3-4 out of 10.
prospect.medical: Sinus and congestion issues when younger, limited running as a result. Right wrist aches under heavy load, managed with stretching and wrist exercises. Recurring neck / upper-back / trap stiffness he attributes to desk posture and sleep position; resolves with stretching. Self-describes sleep cycle as poor and irregular. No diagnoses, medications, surgeries or clinician involvement disclosed.

signals: Proposed label: the_deadline_improver — regularly training, no crisis and no lost former self to recover, but working to a hard external deadline (December wedding) that supplies urgency the rep leans on throughout.
Explicitly frames the goal as good-to-great: 'I would like to get into the fittest shape like I've ever been' and 'I don't want to just restrict it to that level' (the wedding).
Pre-sold on the founder via Instagram and had tried to reach out months earlier — but not via a partner or friend in the programme, so not the_warm_referral.
Price is a real constraint: balked at $6,000, took the $3,000 tier and financed it over instalments, which rules out the_optimizer.

goals.text: Get into the fittest shape of his life, not just wedding-ready
Lose body fat, particularly stubborn belly fat
Build muscle, especially lower body and core
Build stamina so high-intensity work does not leave him gasping
Longevity — stay fit and mobile into later life rather than declining like his parents' generation
Be physically able to play with future children without being restricted
Become someone his partner and family learn from and are motivated by
A nutrition approach that is sustainable through travel, weddings and holidays rather than collapsing after two months
Feel confident in physical activity instead of shying away from it
Look better in his suit on his wedding day in December

pains.text: Cannot sustain motivation to keep going to the gym; life and changing plans derail him
No follow-up or checking from previous paid subscriptions — 'no one would just see what I'm doing'
Plateaus despite regular gym attendance; does not know nutrition, exercise selection or progressive overload
Too many conflicting sources on Instagram and other platforms; ends up nowhere
Previous programmes demanded going zero to 100 at once and were not feasible
Very impromptu, ad-hoc planner — has never held a routine
Low stamina; struggles to sustain HIIT circuits or run
Hesitant and unconfident filming himself training in a public gym because he doubts his form
Right wrist aches under heavy load; recurring neck, trap and upper-back stiffness from posture
Dislikes and cannot sustain daily macro tracking
Gained weight while parents were visiting and has not fully recovered it
Regret looking at photos from a recent family pre-wedding event — 'I so want to not be in this position in my life'
Aware that change gets harder past 30 and does not want to end up where his parents are

objections.raw_quote: Like, I'll have to, like, put in some thought towards it because, yeah, I do see, like, 6K is, like, a big amount, but I also, so it's, like, for the fixed, like, six-month period, like, we have to make the payment up front, all of that, right?
objections.rep_response: Confirmed 'Most guys said we put it all up front, yes.' Did not isolate the objection, did not explore the prospect's financial picture, and did not run the money play. When the prospect proposed starting at the $3,000 tier instead, the rep agreed immediately and also agreed he could upgrade to $6,000 later.

objections.raw_quote: I have seen Trevor, I have seen his work, like, what he talks about, and how he trains and coaches, I've not seen, like, Caden or him, like, or I don't know anything about him, so, if, like, it's possible, like, could you share some, like, yeah, some information or some videos or something of, like, how he works or, like, how he trains, something like that?
objections.rep_response: Did not supply any information, videos or credentials. Asserted equivalence — 'Caden has literally picked up everything that Trevor does. They have the same exact mindset... So they're the same' — then used a reputation-risk rhetorical question, 'do you think he wants to ruin his reputation by working [with someone unqualified]', and finally offered an off-policy refund: 'I'm not really allowed to do this, but... fine, we'll send you your money back.'

objections.raw_quote: Do you think, like, it's possible to also share, like, this information about the light and the different programs over the website or something? Like, if there is a breakdown about, like, what is covered, what not is covered?
objections.rep_response: Told him no written breakdown exists — 'That's not like a whole breakdown or anything, it's basically everything that we've just gone over' — and restated the verbal difference. Proposed label: request_for_written_scope_documentation.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No in-house plan was offered or structured. The prospect self-financed the $3,000 into instalments through Klarna at the checkout: 'So I was trying to set up the Klarna with the multiple payments to break down.' The rep's response was 'We can also do that' and he then sent an alternative processor link before the prospect completed via Klarna anyway.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: No formal guarantee was stated. The rep improvised a refund promise he flagged as off-policy: 'I'm not really allowed to do this, but if you feel like, well, actually, I hate Kay and I don't want to work with him, fine, we'll send you your money back.'

evidence: Payment completed live on the call: 'Okay. I think I've got this through. Oh, my payment went through the chart now.'
Identity verification completed and confirmed: 'Yeah, I'm saying like it's done. It's done.'

Paid via Klarna and sent the rep a receipt screenshot on WhatsApp — corroborated by the same-day internal call with Angelo DiMaggio, where the rep confirms a 3K Klarna payment and asks for the contract automation to be fired.
Onboarding call with Trevor booked live for Monday 1:15 PM Pacific.
Counter-evidence: the contract / agreement email had not arrived by the end of the recording and nothing was signed on the call — the rep left to chase it and the transcript ends there.
Counter-evidence: the amount collected is $3,000, half the standard six-month price, on a 'Kettlebell Body Lite' tier delivered by an assistant coach rather than Trevor.
Counter-evidence: the prospect asked twice for evidence about the coach who would actually deliver the service and paid without receiving any.
outcome.next_step: Sign the agreement email once it arrives, then attend the onboarding call with Trevor on Monday at 1:15 PM Pacific. Rep also shared his personal WhatsApp number for direct contact.

notable.note: Closed at $3,000 on a 'Kettlebell Body Lite' tier that appears nowhere in the documented offer, introduced by the rep immediately alongside the $6,000 tier as a two-option choice rather than after a money play. The prospect's only price hesitation was resolved by halving the price rather than by any scripted objection handling. He then twice asked for evidence about Caden, the assistant coach who will actually deliver the coaching he is paying for, received none, and was closed with an explicitly off-policy refund promise. Age was never asked and is only approximated by the prospect himself ('now because I'm already like, post 30, like 31, 32'); height and weight were never taken at all, so there is no baseline for a body-composition programme. Recording ends mid-process with the agreement unsigned; the immediate continuation is the internal call with Angelo DiMaggio (drive id 1Y-aXDhdR0G1k6eMNYaAj-YoL8NsaajYO).

quality.notes: Severe and sustained label inversion. Long passages of the rep's pillar presentation (roughly 00:32:00-00:38:55) are attributed to 'Dhairya', and several of the rep's discovery questions appear under the prospect's label (e.g. 'What specifically about Trevor makes you be confident that you can actually get the output with him?' at 00:12:08 and 'What are the main factors telling you it's like a 3 or 4?' at 00:14:54). The prospect also changes label mid-call from 'Dhairya Nanda' to 'Dhairya' at 00:01:38 after rejoining from his phone — same person. All roles here were assigned from content, not labels. Audio quality problems in the first 90 seconds also produced garbled and duplicated lines.
